paper_metadata.title: Presurgical seizure frequency and tumoral etiology predict the outcome after extratemporal epilepsy surgery

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population (Bethel Epilepsy Center), recruitment period (1991-2001), and specific inclusion/exclusion criteria (lesional focal extratemporal epilepsy, drug resistance). Baseline characteristics including age, onset, and histology are well-documented.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While most factors (age, histology) are objective, 'seizure frequency' relies on patient reporting and retrospective calculation, which is prone to recall bias. However, the methods for calculation are clearly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: the term seizure frequency reflects the seizure load per year, calculated by multiplying the daily frequency by 365, the weekly frequency by 52 or the monthly frequency by 12.
items.reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (seizure frequency) is explicitly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: If a patient reported repetitive tonic or clonic jerks, a series was counted as one seizure... All seizure types but auras were considered
items.reasoning: Measurement relies on patient self-reporting, which is standard but carries inherent recall bias risk.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariate analysis to adjust for demographic and histologic factors.
